purpose: Primary-source claim ledger; reported literature results are not local replications or global-TV certificates.

paper.title: A fast and frugal Gaussian boson sampling emulator
paper.version_scope: Final publication metadata, abstract, captions and indexed full-text passages covering experimental comparisons, TV limitations, implementation resources and data availability were verified. Details not confirmed in final text remain explicitly tied to the author preprint; no unobserved final-version changes are assumed.

claims.reported_paraphrase: Classical samples match or improve established experimental benchmarks on a CPU/GPU.
claims.scope: Benchmark scores against a chosen lossy ground-truth model.

claims.reported_paraphrase: The authors explicitly omit Jiuzhang1 benchmarking, citing prior reproduction of most of its advantage evidence using unentangled squashed Gaussian states.
claims.scope_note: This explains their benchmark selection; it does not assert full-distribution reproduction of the Jiuzhang1 hardware. Our same-input Jiuzhang1 control is a distinct local experiment.
Postselected XEB sectors do not constitute an unconditional full-law TV bound.

version_evidence.final: 144-mode Jiuzhang comparisons, double-elision K=5, J2-P65-2, photon density .093, cumulants through order five and XEB confirmed.
version_evidence.preprint_detail: The explicit 4000 samples per XEB sector is retained from the preprint.

claims.reported_paraphrase: J2-P65-5: cumulants and total-click histogram; XEB omitted at relevant C>40.
claims.scope_note: Good low-order correlations and a count marginal do not identify the joint distribution.

claims.reported_paraphrase: J3-high is coarse-grained from 1152 detection bins to 144 binary outputs.
claims.scope_note: A separately named coarse-grained task is meaningful; it is not the complete eight-bin pseudo-PNR task.

version_evidence.final: The 144 spatial modes, eight time bins per output, actual 1152-bin task, reduced 144-bit test, high-click XEB cost and retained witness types are explicit in final text.

claims.reported_paraphrase: All cumulants through order four; a 1/24 subset at order five; 100 bootstrap resamples for correlations.
claims.scope_note: The subset and bootstrap are finite witness procedures, not all high-order correlations.

claims.reported_paraphrase: Large-system full TV is not efficiently evaluated; K is chosen heuristically.
claims.scope_note: No numerical full-TV value, epsilon guarantee, or theorem is fabricated from witness acceptance.

version_evidence.final: The final comparison section explains that full-law TV estimation is impractical at the experimental size and uses established metrics.
version_evidence.preprint_detail: The heuristic K-selection statement is retained from the preprint.

claims.reported_paraphrase: Ten million samples in 115 minutes on eight H100 SXM 80 GB GPUs.
claims.scope_note: This is a reported sample-generation time; a fully matched end-to-end timing boundary has not been established here.

version_evidence.final: Final Implementation confirms the ten-million/115-minute/eight-H100 benchmark and EPYC 9654 CPU platform.

claims.reported_paraphrase: The paper's workflow figure gives approximately ten seconds for ten million quantum samples.
claims.inference: 6900/10 is approximately 690, with classical generation slower in that schematic comparison.
claims.scope_note: The schematic does not specify a matched calibration, acceptance protocol or all timing boundaries; it cannot support a precise end-to-end speedup claim.

claims.reported_paraphrase: Phase I depends on M,K; Phase II computes instance-dependent cumulants before sampling.
claims.scope_note: Count both stages for a new instance, with an explicitly stated amortization policy. Synthetic scaling plots are not new hardware-instance benchmarks.

claims.reported_paraphrase: At M=144,K=5: approximately 2 GB cumulants, 2.5 GB auxiliary indices, and 2 MB per sampling thread.
claims.scope_note: Two GB is not total peak memory. The library default alone does not prove the precision used in the publication.

version_evidence.final: Final Implementation confirms 2 GB of cumulants per GPU and approximately 2 MB of per-thread sampling tables.
version_evidence.preprint_detail: The additional 2.5 GB auxiliary-index figure is retained from the preprint.
version_evidence.library_only: The source default is single precision; this is not proof of the publication arithmetic setting.

claims.reported_paraphrase: Scaling to Jiuzhang4 is proposed as future work requiring implementation and numerical improvements.
claims.scope_note: No 8176-output benchmark or full-JZ4 distribution certificate was found in the audited results.
